subject: Proposal: Dedicated pool expansion + temporary SLA rider request
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Voss <ellen.voss@gammahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal + Dedicated pool expansion — capacity/latency asks

Hi Ellen,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a refreshed quote for Gamma's Dedicated renewal that includes the additional reserved pool (4x A100 equivalents) and a higher baseline throughput allowance to support the new inference-heavy workloads on the clinical search pipeline.

Key points in the package:
- 4 additional GPU equivalents in a dedicated reserved pool (adds ~60% peak throughput)
- Guaranteed baseline throughput: 1.2M tokens/day with bursting to 1.8M tokens/day for short windows
- 12-month renewal term with preferred pricing for the incremental capacity (see Gamma_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf)

Operational ask from your side that we discussed: because adding this level of reserved capacity routes a portion of traffic to older quantized variants during scale events, we'd like to include a short-term SLA rider for the first 90 days post-activation to set expectations around latency SLOs and uptime credits while we tune the workload and routing policies. Proposed temporary rider (draft attached: SLA_Rider-draft.docx):
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile target 220ms (rather than our standard 180ms) for 90 days post-activation
- Uptime credit: if monthly uptime falls below 99.5% in that period, Gamma receives a service credit of 5% of monthly committed fees; below 99.0% -> 15% credit
- Weekly tuning checkpoints between Redwood SRE and Gamma infra for first 4 weeks

If that temporary carve-out looks acceptable, we'll route the rider to legal for a short signature and coordinate a firm activation date. If you'd prefer to keep the standard SLA, we can discuss additional runbook/burst capacity as an alternative mitigant.

Attachments: Gamma_Dedicated_Quote_v3.pdf (PDF), SLA_Rider-draft.docx (DOCX), network_topology.png (PNG)

Next step: are you able to confirm procurement path and whether DocuSign is preferred? Once I have a tentative activation week we can lock the SRE and solutions engineering time.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Ellen Voss <ellen.voss@gammahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Gamma Procurement <procurement@gammahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 09:04:12 -0500
Subject: Re: Renewal + Dedicated pool expansion — capacity/latency asks

Neha —

Thanks for the detailed package and the quick turnaround. High level: Gamma is supportive of the expansion; the additional throughput is exactly what our ML infra team needs for next quarter's rollout. A few clarifying notes from procurement/infra: 

1) Procurement: we prefer a 12-month term (same as you propose) and DocuSign is fine. Please include a single consolidated invoice for the reserved capacity line items.

2) Infra: we are concerned about the temporary latency relaxation to 220ms p95 — could you outline exactly which traffic paths might hit the degraded variant during scale events and whether there are mitigations to keep tail latency tighter? Also confirm whether the weekly tuning checkpoints include access to tail-sample logs.

3) SLA credits look reasonable as a backstop, but we'd like to cap the total credits at 30% of the monthly fee across the 90-day onboarding window.

I'll loop in our SRE lead (cc'd procurement) shortly. For timing: target go-live window is the week of Mar 15; can you confirm Redwood's availability for a pre-launch ops dry-run during the week of Mar 8?

Best,
Ellen Voss
Head of Platform Engineering
Gamma Health
ellen.voss@gammahealth.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 14:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Renewal + Dedicated pool expansion — internal notes on SLA rider

Neha —

Quick internal note before we reply to Ellen:

- Engineering feasibility: Solutions engineering confirms the routing that can hit quantized/older variants only during autoscale cold-starts when new instances come up under burst. We can reduce the impact with a staged pre-warm / warm-cache strategy and an initial traffic ramp that holds 40% of burst traffic back for 72 hours. That will likely tighten p95 by ~20-30ms but not entirely eliminate the temporary uplift.

- Logging/access: we should provide Gamma tail-sample access (redacted) and a short-term tracing hook for the 90-day period. Need legal sign-off on log sharing — Marissa, can you take point on a limited data-sharing addendum?

- Credits cap: Acceptable to cap to 30% for the 90-day window, but finance wants the language to reflect 'cumulative credits across the window not to exceed 30% of total committed fees for that period'.

Recommend we propose to Gamma: 1) pre-warm plan + 2) 72-hour gradual ramp + 3) weekly checkpoint + 4) capped credit at 30% — and call out that we expect to hit standard SLA by day 90.

I can join the pre-launch dry-run week of Mar 8 and put solutions engineering on the calendar.

— Jonas
VP, Product Operations (SRE liaison)
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ellen Voss <ellen.voss@gammahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Gamma Procurement <procurement@gammahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal + Dedicated pool expansion — proposal updates and next steps

Ellen —

Appreciate the rapid review. We can accommodate Gamma's asks. Summary of updates based on your notes and internal alignment: 

1) SLA rider: revised language attached to cap cumulative credits at 30% across the 90-day onboarding window. Rider still provides the weekly checkpoints and the credit tiers (below 99.5% -> 5%, below 99.0% -> 15%) but with the cumulative cap.

2) Pre-warm + ramp: Redwood will deliver a pre-warm plan and execute a 72-hour gradual ramp (holdback ~40% of burst traffic initially) — Jonas and the SRE team will run the dry-run.

3) Logs/tracing: We'll provide redacted tail-sample logs and a limited tracing hook for the 90-day period; Marissa will coordinate the limited data-sharing addendum with Gamma legal.

4) Procurement/contract: DocuSign is fine. I'll send the DocuSign package with the consolidated invoice and the revised SLA rider attached by EOD Monday.

Can we lock the dry-run on Mar 9 (preferred) or Mar 10 if that works better for your infra team? Also, please confirm the name and email for the SRE lead so we can provision the trace access.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
